Russia’s elevated crude flows are helping to stoke a supply surplus that’s set to define Bloomberg Terminal
the oil market next year and possibly beyond.
Exports so far this year have averaged 3.65 million barrels a day, the highest annual average since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. That’s even as overseas flows edged lower to 3.92 million barrels a day in the four weeks through Nov. 22, tanker data compiled by Bloomberg showed, down by 30,000 barrels a day from the revised figure for the period to Nov. 15.

This article is for subscribers only.
In the wake of the tech selloff, investors are racing to the safety of Treasuries.
Ten-year Treasury yields have fallen to about 4.85% — despite the risk of higher interest rates as inflation still runs above the Fed’s target. (Meanwhile, gold is acting like the opposite of a haven, with prices sinking closer to $3,500 an ounce.)
“If you want to de-risk your portfolios, Treasuries are quite a natural place for investors to park cash,” said Mark Preskett at Morningstar Wealth. “Yields are pretty attractive at these levels, even in this inflation environment.”

item.title: How Do Europe's Companies Regain Their Edge?
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe • Nov 25th, 2026
How Do Europe's Companies Regain Their Edge?
Europe's industrial companies are under growing pressure from high energy and labor costs, weakening investment and intensifying global competition. McKinsey research finds that 45% of European industrial companies are showing signs of financial stress or distress but argues that the decline is not inevitable. Tunde Olanrewaju, Managing Partner for Europe at McKinsey & Company, joins Bloomberg Radio's Ben Boulos and Charles Capel to discuss what is driving Europe's industrial competitiveness challenge and the turnaround strategies that could help companies fight back.

Gold fell, as a selloff in stocks continued and investors waited for a key inflation print that could shape expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes.
Bullion declined as much as 1.2% to just above $3,500 an ounce, after falling more than 2% on Tuesday. The US personal consumption expenditures price index, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, will give fresh clues on the outlook for monetary policy later Wednesday. A hot print would weigh on non-yielding gold, which generally suffers when borrowing costs rise.

A global selloff in technology stocks is showing no sign of letting up as questions about the outlook for the artificial intelligence trade pile up, with investors turning to bonds for safety.
Nasdaq 100 futures sank 2.4%, pointing to a second straight session of steep losses as traders shunned risk heading into Thanksgiving. S&P 500 contracts fell 1.5%. Nvidia Corp. dropped more than 4% before the open, with all members of the Magnificent Seven trading lower. Anthropic PBC fell below $78 per share.

Advent is considering a bid to acquire French testing firm Bureau Veritas SA, people with knowledge of the matter said, in what would be one of the largest buyouts of a European company this year.
The US private equity firm is working with advisers as it weighs an offer for Bureau Veritas, according to the people. Advent could look to carve out some assets from Bureau Veritas in any deal, they said.

Treasuries rallied across the curve on Wednesday as renewed losses in technology shares dented investor appetite for risk assets.
Yields on benchmark 10-year bonds fell as much as nine basis points to 4.84%, while those on two-year securities more sensitive to policy changes declined eight basis points. The dollar pushed higher.

item.title: ING Sees ‘Full Unwind’ in Emerging-Market Currencies Underway
item.description: Emerging-market currencies face mounting pressure from the technology selloff, the risk of shrinking interest rate premiums and the threat of fresh global tariffs, according to strategists at ING Bank.

item.title: EasyJet Profit Hit By Iran War as Apollo Takeover Looms
item.description: EasyJet Plc said the fallout from Middle East war eroded most of its profit in the fiscal year, with soaring fuel prices hitting the budget carrier as it prepares to be taken over by a US private equity firm early next year.

item.title: Dangote Hires Veteran Oil Trader Jonathan Zarembok From Equinor
item.description: Veteran oil trader Jonathan Zarembok is joining Dangote Group, which has a huge refinery in Nigeria and is expanding elsewhere in Africa, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Danantara Reports $634 Billion Assets in Audited Accounts
item.description: Indonesia’s Danantara reported about $634 billion in consolidated assets at the end of 2025 in its first audited accounts, well below the roughly $1 trillion officials have often cited for the state investment agency central to President Prabowo Subianto’s overhaul of government-owned companies in Southeast Asia’s largest economy.

item.title: Deutsche Bank Is Among Biggest S&P 500 Bulls With 9,000 Target
item.description: Deutsche Bank AG’s Binky Chadha is among the most bullish stock forecasters on Wall Street, predicting the S&P 500 will recover from its rout to rally 25% by the end of next year.
